messages:
Sam: Hey folks — trying to land my first PR. Small bugfix in infra/serve. Quick questions:
- Which branch should I target (main vs feature/*)?
- Commit message format? squash or rebase?
- CI failing locally on `lint` and some flaky tests — what's the best local workflow and who should I ping?

Thanks!

Mira: Welcome! A few quick rules to follow:
- Urgent bugfixes that need immediate deploy -> target `main` (use `hotfix/` prefix).
- Anything non-trivial -> create `feature/<short-desc>` off `main`.

Commit msgs: One-line subject with scope, e.g. `fix(serve): handle nil kv-cache on cold start`. Add a blank line and body if needed. For tiny one-off fixes squash is fine; for multi-step changes keep logical commits and prefer `rebase and merge` at merge time.

Local CI: run `./scripts/local-ci.sh` or `make test-fast` before pushing. If you still see failures, paste the failing command and output here and ping who you think owns the area.

Lina: Quick PR checklist and commands:
- PR title format: `area: short summary` (include Jira like `ENG-1234` if applicable).
- Add labels: `team/runtime`, `area/serve`, `needs-review`.
- Required checks: `unit-tests`, `lint`, `typecheck`, `integration`.

Commands we use locally:
```
./scripts/local-ci.sh --fast
git config --local commit.template ./.git/commit-template.txt
```
If `lint` fails, run `npx eslint --fix` (or `gofmt`/`golines` for Go files) then re-run the local script.

DevEx Bot: [ci-bot] build 2140001111 started for branch feature/sam-first-pr
Checks: unit-tests (running), lint (queued), typecheck (queued)
Link: http://ci.redwood.internal/build/2140001111

Ada: Reviewer guide: ping @Mira for infra/runtime changes, @Lina for style/formatting, @Olivia for API surface. If touching serving perf, also cc @Ben. Add label `reviewer:team-runtime` when you request reviews so the right team sees it.

Sam: Thanks — one more: snapshots in tests. Should I update snapshots locally or remove them to make CI faster?

Mira: Update snapshots locally with `yarn test -u` and include the updates in your PR. Don't remove snapshot tests. If a test is flaky open a small ticket and mark the PR with `flaky-test` so we can triage; we treat flaky tests differently in CI.

Sam: Awesome, will run the scripts, fix lint, update snapshots, and post the PR link when ready. Appreciate the help :thumbsup:
